validation.command: pnpm exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/supervision.test.ts tests/integration/runner-authentication.test.ts
validation.evidence: 2 files and 55 tests passed, including approval races, restart reconciliation, authenticated runner fencing, pre-offer cancellation, and durable capacity projection.
Format, lint and boundaries, lockfile integrity, immutable image pins, secret scan, typecheck, 75 unit tests, 60 contract tests, and 79 integration tests passed.
9 of 9 Chromium tests passed, including approve/apply-once, reject/expiry, and distinct pause, resume, stop, and cancel journeys.
Generated TypeScript derivatives reproduce from the approved OpenAPI and runner protocol contracts.
The bounded US2 specification, plan, tasks, implementation, tests, and evidence contain no remaining actionable gap; T047+ was not evaluated as current work.

approvalEvidence.beforeDecision: The sensitive fixture action persists policy intent and an immutable action-digest approval while the external effect remains REQUESTED and unapplied.
approvalEvidence.authority: Only the configured supervisor actor can decide; specialist self-approval, stale versions, digest tampering, expiry, rejection, cancellation, and budget exhaustion cannot authorize execution.
approvalEvidence.concurrency: Concurrent and duplicate decisions serialize transactionally and converge on one canonical approval outcome and at most one effect attempt.

effectLedgerEvidence.transport: The loopback runner requires mutually authenticated TLS and an exact enrolled URI identity before domain handling.
effectLedgerEvidence.binding: Every offer, query, and cancellation is bound to stable effect, digest, execution, lease, and fencing-token authority.
effectLedgerEvidence.oneShot: Accepted leases are durably consumed before effect application; replay and stale authority are rejected without a duplicate ledger entry.
effectLedgerEvidence.groundTruth: The queryable durable fixture ledger reconciles APPLIED, NOT_APPLIED, and indeterminate outcomes after control-plane or runner interruption.

stopRaceEvidence.preOfferFence: A durable cancellation tombstone records the highest revoked authority even when STOP arrives before the delayed offer, so the same or older offer is rejected after restart.
stopRaceEvidence.inFlight: Pause, stop, and cancel revoke lease authority before reconciliation; indeterminate ground truth remains BLOCKED and retains runner capacity until resolved.
stopRaceEvidence.terminalSemantics: STOP is recoverable through a successor execution with fresh authority, CANCEL is terminal, and optimistic project versions make the first committed completion/control transition win.

auditEvidence.attribution: Policy, tool intent, approval request/decision, effect attempt/result, and control receipt/completion records carry one attributable actor, correlation identity, target, reason, and outcome.
auditEvidence.exactlyOnce: Transactional command idempotency and projection tests prevent duplicate logical audit identities under retries and races.
auditEvidence.privacy: Public fixture projections contain bounded summaries and omit private reasoning, credentials, authorization material, raw prompts, and host-sensitive paths.

capacityAndTimeEvidence.authorityClock: Approval and lease validity use PostgreSQL clock_timestamp() inside the authoritative mutation transaction.
capacityAndTimeEvidence.globalReservation: Cross-instance runner reservation serializes on a PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock; a delayed first effect projects 1/1, a second waits without crossing its boundary, and determinate release projects 0/1.
capacityAndTimeEvidence.failClosed: UNKNOWN and RECONCILING effects continue to occupy the single runner slot until durable ground truth is known.

independentReview.reviewedRisks: Approval authority, PostgreSQL time and capacity, idempotent ledger recovery, STOP-before-offer fencing, mTLS identity, one-shot lease consumption, runner-capacity projection, contract/UI consistency, secrets, and remote effects.
